title: CaptureEvidence
description: What an instrumentation sends back for a capture the cloud asked for (POST /v0/captures/{id}/evidence). It is the contents of the black box, frozen: the fine register's requests with their operations, in order, with starts and ends, and the coarse summary of the previous minutes, second by second. Hashes only — the text of a query never travels here (invariant 5). Its own path and not the aggregates batch, because a batch is what goes out every ten seconds and this is a rare event several orders of magnitude larger.

protocol.description: Protocol version this payload conforms to. Same enum as a batch: every published minor of v0 stays acceptable.

instance.description: Which process observed this. Several instances of one deployment get the same order on purpose (ADR 0071), so the cloud has to be able to tell two answers apart.

startedAt.description: The **effective start of observation**, which is the instant CAP-01 insists on keeping apart from the acceptance. It travels with the evidence rather than in a call of its own: a capture that started and never finished should not cost two requests.

requests.description: The requests observed, oldest first. An empty array is a real answer and the commonest one: a route nobody called during the window. It means the capture is `empty`, and `product.md:192` is explicit that this must never read as an invitation to ask again unchanged.

Coverage.title: CaptureCoverage
Coverage.description: `product.md:192` asks a capture to declare **both** coverages: what it attached from detail still retained, and what it observed from its effective start. Two numbers, never one — a total would hide that half of it is older than the capture.

observedRequests.description: Requests seen from the effective start onwards.

attachedRequests.description: Requests that were already in the register when the capture started, and are attached. Zero is normal: the register may have wrapped, and nothing brings back what was not kept.

detailLost.description: Requests whose operations were overwritten before they could be read. Their timing is still true; what is gone is the detail. Reported rather than dropped, because a request with no operations reads as one that ran nothing (invariant 14).

truncated.description: Requests that ran more operations than the register keeps per request. Their count is real and their list is not complete.

route.description: The route template, never the path with its values in it (invariant 5).

startedAt.description: When this request started. Absolute, so requests from two instances can be read side by side.

poolWaitMs.description: How long this request waited for a connection from a pool before it could talk to the dependency at all. **Absent means this request asked no pool**, which is not a wait of zero: zero is a request that asked and was served at once. The pool-saturation trigger compares wait per request, so a route that never queues must not read as one that queues for nothing (invariant 14).

operations.description: What it ran, in the order it started them. Empty means it ran nothing — unless `detailLost` says the list was overwritten, which is why that flag is on the request and not only in the totals.

truncated.description: This request ran more operations than the register keeps per request. Absent means false.

detailLost.description: This request's operations were overwritten before they were read. Absent means false. Its timing is still true.

CapturedOperation.title: CapturedOperation
CapturedOperation.description: One operation inside a request. Starts and ends and not durations, because the whole reason for capturing detail is order and overlap, which a duration cannot express (ADR 0068).

hash.description: The fingerprint's hash. Never the text: the profile is where a sender chooses whether to ship the text of its queries, and this path never carries it (invariant 5, ADR 0017).

startMs.description: Milliseconds from the start of its own request.

Reference.title: ReferenceSamples
Reference.description: A few requests of each endpoint kept as something to compare the captured ones against. `product.md:100`: «Comparing degraded requests against reference requests requires keeping both; the fine detail of an hour ago no longer exists». Being earlier does not certify health, which is why every field here is about how they were chosen and none of them says «healthy».

selection.description: How they were chosen. Travels with them because a sample whose selection is unknown cannot support an attribution (ATR-01). `uniform-reservoir`: every request observed of that endpoint had the same chance of being kept, whatever it did — which is what «the fastest N» would not be.

population.description: How many requests they were drawn from, over the life of the sending process.

routesDropped.description: Endpoints seen that the register had no room for. Counted rather than silently absent: an endpoint with no samples is not an endpoint with no traffic (invariant 14).

renewalPaused.description: True when requests were observed that the register deliberately did not consider. The instrumentation pauses renewal while it is watching a capture, which is the closest it can get to REF-01 from inside the process: it cannot know whether an incident is open, but it knows detail has been asked of it. Absent means false.

samples.description: The kept requests, in the same shape as the captured ones. An empty array is a real answer: a process that has just started has nothing to compare with yet.

CoarseSummary.title: CoarseSummary
CoarseSummary.description: The coarse half of the black box, frozen: the last few minutes, second by second, so a reader can see how something detected late began (`product.md:94`). Sums and a maximum, never percentiles: the interval aggregate answers the percentile question with exactness, and this answers the shape of the change (`product.md:122`). What an older instrumentation did not send is absent from the evidence, and stored as absent.

windowSeconds.description: How many seconds the summary covers: the length of the register's window, and the most any of the lists below may hold.

routesDropped.description: Routes the register had no row for, folded into one shared row, counted once each. At the register's cap for how many it may remember it is a lower bound: a bounded memory does not count distinct names past its bound, and the volume of what was folded is what the shared row keeps.

routes.description: One entry per route with a row of its own, the last being the shared row for what did not fit, when there is one. A route's series starts at the first second this process saw the route: before it, nobody was watching this route, and inventing silence there would say the route was quiet when the truth is that it was unwatched (invariant 14).

eventLoop.description: The process's event loop delay, second by second, in its own series and not attributed to any route: it is the process's, and attributing it to a route would be inventing a measurement. Only the seconds somebody sampled are here: a second with no reading says nothing about the loop, and a zero would say it was idle. An empty array is a real answer: the process had no event loop to sample, or nobody did.

route.description: The route template, never the path with its values in it (invariant 5).

CoarseSecond.title: CoarseSecond
CoarseSecond.description: One second of one route. Sums and a maximum, never a histogram: a histogram per second per route would multiply the memory by its buckets to answer a question the interval already answers.

second.description: The Unix second this row covers, an integer instant like the ones a batch writes: a reader aligns it with the dates the evidence writes by flooring them.

requests.description: Requests this route answered in this second. Zero is a real answer: a watched second with no traffic, and not an absence.

calls.description: Operations the requests of this second ran.

second.description: The Unix second this reading covers.

maxDelayMs.description: The worst delay sampled in this second: a second that stalled once stalled, and averaging it away is how a stall becomes invisible.
